The house standard asks for a probable rule referenced from the priority evaluation where the red box names a likely diagnosis for a subset of criteria. SBP < 80 alone is still caught by the measurement clause, but pulse/RR/confusion/weakness do nothing.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: drug rash with markers of severity
rule_level_problems.problem: The page carries two BP thresholds (red box: SBP < 80; footnote 2 markers of severity: BP < 90/60). The rule includes both, so SBP < 80 is subsumed by SBP < 90 and the effective Urgent threshold is the footnote's. This follows the page's own definition of 'markers of severity' and is not wrong, but it should be a recorded decision since it makes the red box's stated SBP < 80 redundant.

rule_level_problems.rule: Suspect drug rash: generalised rash after new medication
rule_level_problems.problem: The 3-month window is measured from medication start to now, not to rash onset as the page says. The language cannot compare two onsets, so this is the closest encoding; a late presenter (drug started > 3 months ago, rash appeared within 3 months of starting) will not get the possible diagnosis and so will not trigger the severity check_for.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for new medication in generalised rash
rule_level_problems.problem: The whole chain starts from (clinical_finding Generalized rash disorder), which is not a common symptom or warning sign in the house list. If the nurse records a parent or sibling rash concept (e.g. 'Eruption of skin' or a non-generalised rash) nothing on this page fires. Reasonable per the page wording ('generalised rash'), but worth a remaining-questions note.

The page places 'fixed drug eruption likely' only in the 'No' branch (patient not on ART/TB medication/co-trimoxazole/TPT); the rule applies to any drug rash. Clinically defensible (fixed drug eruption is not drug-class specific) and the branch is routing, but it is a departure from the page's layout.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded: every one of the 11 criteria (split into 23 parts) matches an existing SNOMED concept or vital-sign threshold in the Urgent priority rule, and the check_for mirrors it with no unused items. The one substantive miss is footnote 1's 'shock likely' definition, which has no probable Shock rule, so pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness and weakness never contribute to the Urgent evaluation. Lesser points: the 3-month window is anchored to now rather than rash onset (a language limit), SBP < 80 is made redundant by the footnote's BP < 90/60, and the fixed drug eruption rule is not restricted to the page's 'No' branch.
